questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks does the body eliminate per hour?
questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour. Blood alcohol content (BAC) lowers at different rates for different people. It is safest not to drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: If a dog chases you on your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Stop until the animal loses interest.
Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Downshift and slowly approach the dog. Once you are close, accelerate and leave it behind. Do not kick at the dog.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
Rely on your mirrors to show you all of your surroundings.
Point in the direction of the lane change.
Speed up to get ahead of other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: Which surface provides the best traction for a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce traction for motorcycles. Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal plates are all hazardous. Dry pavement is the safest.

questions.question: As you slow or stop, you should:

options.text: Take the bike out of gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift down through the gears.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears using the clutch as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: When adjusting your mirrors, you should focus on:

options.text: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
The road in front of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane beside you. You may see part of your arm or shoulder, but seeing the road behind and beside you is most important.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate in groups. When the lead rider extends their left arm straight down with their palm facing back, it means the group should stop.

questions.question: If you ride alongside another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Stay alongside the vehicle until the next exit and then exit.
Let the other driver worry about it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up or slow down.
questions.explanation: Riding directly next to another vehicle is dangerous. You could be in their blind spot, and they could block your escape route if a hazard appears. Speed up or drop back.

questions.question: When should you use the front brake?

options.text: Any time you are slowing or stopping
Only when slowing or stopping on slippery roads
Only when slowing or stopping in an emergency
Only when slowing or stopping in traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time you are slowing or stopping
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow or stop.

questions.question: Where is the engine cut-off switch usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The engine cut-off switch is located next to the right handgrip. Know where all your motorcycle controls are before you ride.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a good way for a rider to increase visibility?

options.text: Using your headlight at all times

questions.correctAnswerText: Waving at other drivers
questions.explanation: To stay visible, wear bright clothing with reflective materials, use your headlight at all times, and use your signals and brake light correctly.

questions.question: Why is riding directly next to another vehicle dangerous?

options.text: You may have a hard time reaching a highway exit.
You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It prevents other drivers from passing both of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not see you in their blind spot. The driver could turn into your lane without warning. Also, the vehicle blocks your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, what should you do?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handles.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If one tire goes flat, grip both handles firmly, ease off the throttle, and keep going straight. If you must brake, slowly apply the brake on the good tire. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: Where is the clutch lever usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the left handlebar
questions.explanation: The clutch lever on a motorcycle is usually located on the left handlebar.

questions.question: What does it mean if a driver makes eye contact with you?

options.text: It does not mean they will properly yield to you.
It guarantees they will properly yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean they will properly yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not count on eye contact to guarantee a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcycles but fail to notice them.

questions.question: How can a motorcyclist prevent other vehicles from sharing their lane?

options.text: Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the center portion of the lane.
Give dirty looks if another driver enters your lane.
Ride in a zigzag pattern to fill up the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center portion of your lane to discourage drivers from trying to squeeze in next to you.

questions.question: At night, how should your following distance compare to daytime riding?

options.text: Allow a longer following distance at night.
Allow a shorter following distance at night.
Always maintain the same following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow a longer following distance at night.
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to judge distance because shadows and light contrasts are missing or unclear. You should allow more following distance at night than during the day.

questions.question: What should you do if another vehicle is tailgating you?

options.text: Allow the other driver to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the other driver to pass you.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them ahead of you. If safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may cause them to tailgate at a higher speed, making it more dangerous.

questions.question: What happens to the steering if your front tire goes flat?

options.text: The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The steering will feel heavy.
questions.explanation: If the front tire goes flat, the steering will feel heavy. If your steering feels heavy, exit the road immediately and check your tires.

questions.question: How often should you check your mirrors while riding?
questions.correctAnswerText: Frequently
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors frequently to be aware of vehicles and hazards behind you.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Ignore them and focus on the road ahead.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Move onto the shoulder and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate faster, which is more dangerous. Never ride on the shoulder because other drivers won't expect you there and may suddenly leave the road.

questions.question: Why is a leather jacket important for motorcycle riding?

options.text: It makes a rider look cool.
It is usually too warm to wear.
It protects you in a crash.
You should not wear one while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved jacket made of leather when riding. Leather protects you from injury in a crash. In hot weather, leather jackets also help prevent dehydration. Many motorcycle jackets are made to keep you cool even in warm weather.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective riding gear?
questions.correctAnswerText: Pants made of soft material
questions.explanation: Good protective gear includes a leather jacket and sturdy pants, boots that cover your ankles, and hearing protection. Soft material pants do not protect you in a crash.

questions.question: How should you sit on a motorcycle to control it properly?

options.text: Sit so your arms control the steering, not hold you up.
Sit far back on the seat with your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Drag your feet on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so your arms control the steering, not hold you up.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms steer the motorcycle instead of holding you up. Your arms should be slightly bent when gripping the handlebars. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet on the footrests to maintain balance.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle on a two-lane road, how should they pass?

options.text: Pass in a staggered formation with several riders at once.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass one at a time.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, motorcycle riders should pass one at a time. Each rider must finish passing before the next rider begins.
